newsitem.title: UK: FORECASTS CUT AS REED H1 DISAPPOINTS.
newsitem.headline: FORECASTS CUT AS REED H1 DISAPPOINTS.

text.p: Analysts cut their full-year forecasts for Reed Elsevier on Thursday after the company's interim results came in at the bottom end of expectations.

"The underlying performance is pretty solid but higher development costs and sterling are squeezing profits," said Anthony de Larrinaga of Panmure Gordon. He cut his 1997 pre-tax profit forecast to 840 million stg from 870 million.
Reed shares fell 32p to 598p by 1230 GMT after the company unveiled a mere one percent rise in first half profit to 419 million stg.
"The underlying position is very healthy. They have the content, the management and the resources," said de Larrinaga.

Louise Barton of Henderson Crosthwaite trimmed her 1997 forecast to 830 million stg from 857 million, citing higher development costs, a pension accounting provision and the impact of the strong pound.
Reed said sterling wiped 36 million stg from profit in the first half and said the effect would be broadly similar in the second half if the pound remained at current high levels.

Another analyst, who did not want to be named, said he was cutting his forecast by 23 million stg to 840 million and looking for 900 million stg next year, down from an earlier estimate of 939 million.
